newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices firm on higher Tokyo futures.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices firm on higher Tokyo futures.

text.p: Thai rubber prices edged up on the back of higher Tokyo futures but overall demand remained soft, trade sources said on Friday.
Japan and China made enquiries, but only Japan bought, they told Reuters. Thai benchmark RSS3 was indicated at 108.50 US cents per kg FOB Bangkok from 106.00 a week earlier.
The government scrapped its bid for 2,000 tonnes of RSS4 rubber, saying offers of 108.00-120.00 US cents a kg were too high. However, it bought 3,500 tonnes of RSS3 earlier this week.
A senior agricultural ministry official said the government had bought 45,000 tonnes from the local market so far since March to prop up prices and intended to buy more.
Traders lashed out at the government's plan to raise the minimum guaranteed prices for grade-3 sheet rubber to 29.00 baht from 27.50 baht earlier.
The move came after rubber tappers in several southern provinces held a protest, demanding the hike.
"It seemed like this government succumbed to demand of any mob whose number exceeded 1,000," said one Hat Yai trader.
"But what the govenrnment did distorted the market. World prices are bearish. We will have difficulties meeting obligations now that the local prices are high," he said.
The government used a two-throng approach to help shore up prices. It guaranteed minimum prices for local tappers and bought directly from the domestic FOB market.
